items.title: Hundreds of thousands lose power after Thanksgiving storms
items.feedTitle: Thousands still without power after Thanksgiving storms
items.summary: A powerful storm system battered the US Northeast and West Coast on Thanksgiving, leaving approximately 490,000 customers without power as of Friday afternoon, with the most severe outages in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. Power restoration efforts are ongoing as residents deal with spoiled food and disrupted travel plans. The storm also caused widespread flooding and downed trees across multiple states from Maine to Florida.

items.title: Senator Deb Fischer's husband died by suicide
items.feedTitle: Sen. Deb Fischer's office says her husband died by suicide
items.summary: A spokesperson for Senator Deb Fischer (R-Neb.) confirmed that her husband, Bruce Fischer, died by suicide earlier in the week. The announcement came after the senator's office released a statement Friday noting the tragic update on his death.

items.title: US military disables vessel breaching Iranian naval blockade
items.feedTitle: Military says it disabled vessel that 'attempted to run the U.S. naval blockade' against Iran
items.summary: US Central Command reported that American forces fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday, disabling the ship's propulsion after it attempted to breach the US naval blockade of Iranian ports despite multiple warnings. The civilian crew was unharmed in the strike.

items.title: Trump to attend semiconductor facility groundbreaking in Phoenix
items.feedTitle: Trump to visit groundbreaking for semiconductor manufacturer that supplies Nvidia: Reports
items.summary: President Trump is reportedly set to attend the groundbreaking of a new semiconductor manufacturing facility in Phoenix that will produce chips for Nvidia and other companies. The facility represents a significant investment in US semiconductor production capacity amid ongoing industry competition.

items.title: Record Black Friday spending expected despite inflation concerns
items.feedTitle: Weeks of hot deals are encouraging record Black Friday spending despite inflation concerns
items.summary: Retail experts predict record Black Friday spending this year as consumers engage in extensive holiday shopping despite lingering concerns about inflation. Physical stores are experiencing strong foot traffic, with Sensormatic Solutions reporting Black Friday remains the highest-traffic retail day despite e-commerce growth and earlier online discounting.

stlouis.title: St. Louis area power outages persist; restoration could take days
stlouis.feedTitle: Ameren said it will still take a few days to restore power to some as nearly 80,000 customers remain without power
stlouis.summary: Nearly 80,000 customers in the St. Louis region remained without power following the Thanksgiving winter storm. Ameren said restoration efforts could take several more days, with heavy wet snow and downed trees causing widespread damage across the area.

stlouis.title: St. Louis records second-snowiest Thanksgiving in storm history
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis Got 7.3 Inches of Heavy, Wet Snow, Its Second-Snowiest Thanksgiving Storm on Record. Missouri’s Extension Forester Says Damaged Trees Deserve Patience.
stlouis.summary: St. Louis received 7.3 inches of heavy, wet snow on Thanksgiving, marking the second-snowiest Thanksgiving storm on record. The Missouri Extension Forester advises residents to exercise patience with damaged trees, which will require time to recover from the weather stress.

stlouis.title: St. Louis residents can seek reimbursement for spoiled food from outages
stlouis.feedTitle: Spoiled food from a St. Louis-area power outage? You could seek reimbursement
stlouis.summary: Residents in the St. Louis area who lost food due to power outages from the Thanksgiving storm may be eligible to seek reimbursement. Local authorities have announced options for compensation as thousands dealt with the aftermath of widespread blackouts.

items.title: Russian sabotage in Europe risks mass-casualty event, warns thinktank
items.feedTitle: ‘Mass-casualty event’ in Europe possible amid rise in Russian sabotage, says thinktank
items.summary: A European think tank has warned that a potential 'mass-casualty event' could result from a reported rise in Russian-directed sabotage activities across Europe. The report highlights escalating attacks targeting critical infrastructure and Ukrainian supply lines, with incidents increasing 16% according to recent analyses.

items.title: Ukraine braces for another devastating winter amid ongoing war
items.feedTitle: Weary of war but with no sign of backing down, Kyiv faces another punishing winter
items.summary: As freezing weather sets in, Ukraine faces another punishing winter with no clear end to the conflict in sight. Kyiv residents and business owners are preparing for continued bombardments and resource shortages, while questions persist about the ultimate resolution of the two-year-old war.

items.title: Zelenskyy criticises Trump's 'strange' Putin friendship in BBC interview
items.feedTitle: Zelensky criticises 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the BBC he finds Trump's characterization of Putin as 'my friend' strange and troubling, likening it to someone calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War II. Zelenskyy criticized the US for being too focused on the Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough in peace negotiations.

items.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted of additional 123 deaths
items.feedTitle: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
items.summary: Paul Mackenzie, a Kenyan cult leader already serving time for mass murder, has been convicted of killing an additional 123 followers. The convictions add to his previous 191-murder conviction, highlighting the horrific scope of deaths associated with his doomsday cult.

items.title: Canada's top court upholds Quebec religious symbols ban for public servants
items.feedTitle: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
items.summary: Canada's Supreme Court largely upheld a controversial Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols such as hijabs and turbans on the job. The decision exposed tensions between minority rights and government authority, with the law facing challenges from Muslim, Sikh, and Catholic workers.

items.title: Fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
items.feedTitle: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
items.summary: Global fashion brands have diverted approximately $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh to India between November 1 and 18 as political unrest disrupts Bangladesh's garment industry. The shift reflects brands' efforts to diversify supply chains away from instability in the region's largest apparel exporter.

items.title: DMK sets conditions to support government's delimitation bill
items.feedTitle: NCP-SP announces support to delimitation, Congress calls it ‘unfortunate’
items.summary: The DMK party has announced conditional support for the government's delimitation bill, which proposes redrawing Lok Sabha constituencies. The party's backing contrasts with Congress opposition and deepens intra-coalition tensions over the contentious electoral redistricting exercise.

items.title: India-US trade deal nearing completion, minister says
items.feedTitle: India-US trade deal is nearing completion, minister says
items.summary: India's commerce minister has stated that a comprehensive trade deal with the United States is close to completion after months of negotiations. The minister indicated that key procedural obstacles, which had previously delayed finalization, are now being resolved.

items.title: Indian police rescue 164 foreigners from cyberfraud racket in Noida
items.feedTitle: Noida: 164 foreigners rescued from cyberfraud racket
items.summary: Indian authorities rescued 164 foreign nationals who were trafficked into an international cyberfraud operation in Noida near Delhi. The victims were subjected to fake job recruitment schemes, passport seizure, and threats as part of an elaborate human trafficking and fraud ring.

items.title: Ex-CJI alleges 'complete disregard' for merit in judicial appointments
items.feedTitle: Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President Murmu, alleges ‘complete disregard’ for merit and inclusivity in judicial appointments
items.summary: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai has written to President Murmu alleging that recent judicial appointments show 'complete disregard' for merit and inclusivity. He further claims that a single community represents 40% of Supreme Court appointments despite comprising only 5% of the population.

immigration.title: IBM ends visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles
immigration.feedTitle: IBM to end US visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles
immigration.summary: IBM has announced it is ending US visa and green card sponsorship for most positions in its consulting division, giving affected H-1B and green card holders three weeks to either relocate within the company or leave. The move marks a significant shift in sponsorship policy affecting thousands of international workers, primarily from India.

immigration.title: Department of Labor proposes major PERM labor certification overhaul
immigration.feedTitle: USDOL Plans to Overhaul the PERM Labor Certification Requirements: What Employers Need to Know
immigration.summary: The Department of Labor has proposed sweeping changes to the PERM labor certification process that governs employment-based green card sponsorships. The proposed rule, published in the Federal Register, aims to strengthen standards and protections for US workers in the immigrant visa program and represents the first major modernization of these requirements in years. This is proposed, not final.

immigration.title: H-1B visa appointment delays strand skilled workers abroad
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B visa delays leave skilled workers stranded abroad, says US Congressman
immigration.summary: US Congressman Ro Khanna has raised concerns about significant delays in H-1B visa appointments at State Department consulates, with skilled workers stranded abroad for months unable to begin work in the United States. The delays are attributed to staffing shortages at visa processing facilities, according to GAO data cited by Khanna. This is a pending consequence, not finalized policy.

items.title: Wall Street closes best week in over a year on tech rebound
items.feedTitle: Stock Market News Nov. 27, 2026: Dow zooms higher, clinches best week since 2022 as stocks rebound in holiday-shortened trade
items.summary: US stock markets ended their best week in more than a year as technology stocks rebounded sharply following the volatile trading earlier in the week. The Dow Jones climbed nearly 600 points on Friday to close out the strongest week since 2022, as investor fears over AI sector stability subsided.

items.title: Indian benchmarks snap rally; Sensex falls 989 points amid profit-taking
items.feedTitle: Sensex snaps 2-day rally, tanks 989 points amid profit booking
items.summary: India's stock market benchmarks snapped a 2-day winning streak Friday, with the Sensex declining 989 points as rising crude oil prices and rupee weakness triggered profit-booking across IT and financial stocks. The decline ended a four-week rally that had lifted the Nifty 15%, signaling potential consolidation ahead.

items.title: France slips into recession after two consecutive quarters of GDP decline
items.feedTitle: France Slips Into Recession as Exports Sag
items.summary: France's economy has contracted more than previously estimated, entering technical recession after two consecutive quarters of GDP decline. The contraction reflects weakness in exports and broader economic headwinds affecting the eurozone's second-largest economy.

items.title: Budget airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, cancels all flights
items.feedTitle: Airline Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit declares bankruptcy
items.summary: Norse Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights after surging fuel costs caused by the Iran conflict destroyed its finances. The Norwegian airline advised customers not to come to airports, recommending they pursue refunds through the bankruptcy process, though guarantees are not assured.

items.title: China reserves right to respond to Trump's new tariff proposals
items.feedTitle: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
items.summary: Beijing stated it reserves the right to take 'necessary measures' after the Trump administration proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China and the EU. China characterized the new levies as 'political manipulation,' while Brazil warned it 'will not yield to this type of threat.'

cards.title: Sleep and immune response
cards.insight: The body's ability to fight illness depends heavily on sleep quality. During deep sleep, the immune system releases cytokines that help combat infection and inflammation. Disrupted sleep—whether from stress, travel, or seasonal changes—weakens this natural defense.
cards.takeaway: Prioritize 7-9 hours of consistent sleep, especially during high-stress seasons like the holidays; maintain a regular sleep schedule even when traveling.

cards.title: Movement breaks and cognitive function
cards.insight: Prolonged sitting impairs blood flow to the brain and stiffens muscles, reducing focus and mood. Even 2-3 minute movement breaks every 30-60 minutes restore circulation and mental clarity, without requiring formal exercise.
cards.takeaway: Set hourly reminders to stand, stretch, or walk—this simple habit boosts productivity and prevents the fatigue that comes with desk work.

cards.title: Social connection and stress resilience
cards.insight: Meaningful social interactions activate the parasympathetic nervous system, lowering cortisol and blood pressure. Conversely, isolation amplifies anxiety and depression, especially during darker months when mood is already vulnerable.
cards.takeaway: Schedule regular check-ins with friends or family; even brief phone calls or in-person meetups significantly buffer against seasonal mood decline.

cards.title: Hydration and mental clarity
cards.insight: Even mild dehydration impairs concentration, mood, and energy levels. The brain is 75% water; a 2% fluid loss can noticeably slow cognitive function and increase perception of effort during tasks.
cards.takeaway: Drink water consistently throughout the day, aiming for pale urine; this low-cost intervention is among the most underrated wellness practices.

ai.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets
ai.summary: OpenAI has filed a countersuit against Apple, alleging the tech giant stole trade secrets and pressured hardware suppliers to shun OpenAI devices. The legal action escalates the dispute between the two companies and reveals tensions over AI device development and market access.

ai.title: Anthropic shares jump after volatile IPO week trading
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic likely to join major indexes, but not S&P 500 yet, says TD Securities Peter Haynes
ai.summary: Anthropic's stock surged 11% on Friday as the broader tech sector rebounded, marking volatile trading in the AI startup's first week as a public company following its recent IPO. The company is likely to be added to major stock indexes though not yet the S&P 500, according to analysts.

ai.title: Broadcom's custom AI chips emerge as Nvidia's real rival
ai.feedTitle: Broadcom’s custom AI chips are becoming a real threat to Nvidia
ai.summary: Broadcom's custom-designed AI chips are emerging as a credible competitive threat to Nvidia's dominance in the AI chip market. Industry analysis suggests that hyperscalers developing proprietary silicon represent a more serious challenge to Nvidia than traditional semiconductor competitors like AMD.

ai.title: US works to restrict China's access to advanced AI chips
ai.feedTitle: US works to restrict China’s access to AI chips
ai.summary: The US government is implementing measures to restrict China's access to cutting-edge AI chips as part of broader technology competition strategy. The restrictions aim to limit China's advancement in AI capabilities while protecting US technological leadership in the sector.

ai.title: Elon Musk admits xAI lagging rivals in AI model race
ai.feedTitle: "We can't beat them," Elon Musk publicly conceded defeat in the AI model race, admitted to employees that the company is "lagging behind its rivals" and warned that anyone who wastes GPU resources will be fired.
ai.summary: Elon Musk has publicly acknowledged that his xAI company is 'lagging behind rivals' in the AI model development race and stated 'we can't beat them.' He warned employees that anyone wasting GPU resources would be fired, signaling serious urgency to close the competitive gap.
